title: Who can tell the truth?
prompt: Ada and Ben each either always tell the truth or always lie. Ada says, “We both lie.” Ben says, “The code is 7.” What is the code?

title: Find the only true label
prompt: A key is in one of boxes 7, 8 and 9. The label on 7 says “The key is not here.” The label on 8 says “The key is in box 7.” The label on 9 says “The key is not in box 8.” Exactly one label is true. Which box holds the key?

title: Two statements are false
prompt: A flag is red, blue or green. Mia says it is blue. Niko says it is not green. Both statements are false. What colour is the flag? Enter the colour.

title: Three guesses, two correct statements
prompt: A card shows one of the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4. Ali says it is odd. Bevan says it is greater than 2. Casey says it is 2. Exactly two statements are true. What number is on the card?

title: Three consecutive locker numbers
prompt: Three lockers numbered consecutively have labels that add to 24. What is the middle locker number?

title: Factors at both ends of the card
prompt: A card shows one of the numbers 24, 30, 36 and 42. Its number has exactly nine positive factors and is divisible by 4. Which number is on the card?

title: The missing column total
prompt: A table has three rows and three columns. Its row totals are 12, 17 and 15. Two of its column totals are 11 and 16. What is the remaining column total?

title: The entry that changes its column
prompt: The four row totals in a table add to 70. Its first three column totals add to 49. One entry in the fourth column is then increased by 6. What is the new total of that column?

title: Match a product and a difference
prompt: Two positive whole numbers have product 40 and differ by 3. What is the smaller number?

title: Close to half, but different
prompt: Two different positive even whole numbers total 14. What is the largest possible value of the smaller number?

title: Everyone made a different claim
prompt: A coin is hidden under exactly one cup labelled 1, 2 or 3. Ava says, “It is not under 1.” Ben says, “It is not under 2.” Cora says, “It is under 3.” All three statements have the same truth value. What is the label of the cup with the coin?

title: A single correct route
prompt: A path uses one of four gates, numbered 1 to 4. The signs say “gate 1 or 2”, “gate 2 or 3”, “gate 3 or 4” and “gate 2”. Exactly three signs are correct. Which gate does the path use?

title: The unseen box in a row
prompt: Four numbers sit in a row. The first two add to 15. The last two add to 19. The middle two add to 16. What do the two outside numbers add to?

title: The two diagonals share a centre
prompt: In a square array of nine numbers, the two diagonals each total 18. Together the four corner numbers total 22. What is the centre number?

title: The closest factors with two divisibility rules
prompt: Two different positive whole numbers have product 120. The smaller number is a multiple of 3 and the larger is a multiple of 5. What is the smallest possible larger number?

title: Two rectangles share their area
prompt: A rectangle with whole-number sides has the same area as a second rectangle made by doubling its shorter side and taking 4 cm off its longer side. What was the length of the longer side, in centimetres?

title: One number on the four cards
prompt: A card shows one of 4, 6, 8 and 10. Jules says it is less than 8. Kim says it is more than 4. Lou says it is 8 or 10. Exactly one person is right. What is the number on the card?

title: The truth-teller points elsewhere
prompt: Three people always either tell the truth or lie. Exactly one tells the truth. Ana says, “Ben is the truth-teller.” Ben says, “Ana is the truth-teller.” Cleo says, “Ana and Ben are both liars.” Who is the truth-teller? Enter the name.

title: A total reached by exactly two purchases
prompt: A bakery sells rolls at $3 and buns at $5. In how many different ways can a customer spend exactly $24 while buying at least one of each? Count choices by the numbers of rolls and buns.

title: Build the two sides around a number
prompt: Two different whole numbers larger than 1 multiply to 144. Their sum is less than 40, both are even, and the greater number is four times the smaller. What is the sum of the two numbers?

title: Read the same numbers in two directions
prompt: A square table has two rows and two columns. Its top row totals 17 and its bottom row totals 21. Its left column totals 14. How much larger is the right column total than the left column total?

title: The cell that makes both totals rise
prompt: A grid contains numbers in three rows and three columns. Initially every row and every column sums to 20. One number is erased and replaced by a number 5 larger. What is the sum of all six row and column totals now?

title: Three clues to one cup
prompt: A token lies under one of five cups labelled 1 to 5. Ava says the label is odd. Bo says the label is bigger than 2. Dee says the label is a multiple of 3. All three statements are correct. What is the label?

title: Two clues agree and the other two fail
prompt: A prize is in box 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5. A says it is in an even box. B says the number is greater than 2. C says it is in box 2 or 5. D says it is in a box numbered less than 4. Exactly two statements are true, and one of those is C's. Which box holds the prize?

title: Overlapping strips of three cells
prompt: Five numbers in a row are labelled A, B, C, D and E. The first three add to 27, the last three add to 32, and all five add to 48. What is C?

title: The sum of the two missing corners
prompt: A 2-by-3 table has top row total 20 and bottom row total 25. The middle column totals 14. The top-left number is 7 and the bottom-right number is 10. What is the sum of the other two corner numbers?

title: The common value down every column
prompt: A square grid of numbers has four rows and four columns. The row totals are 15, 21, 18 and 26. The four columns all have the same total. What is one column total?

title: The diagonal is counted three times
prompt: The nine entries of a 3-by-3 grid total 48. The totals of its three rows, three columns and two long diagonals add to 127. The centre entry is 6. What is the sum of the four corner entries?
